adventure.title: Tibidabo's Cliff-Edge Ferris Wheel
adventure.description: Ride a 1920s fairground wheel bolted to the top of a mountain, with the whole city and the Mediterranean dropping away beneath your feet.
adventure.bonus: Ride the Avió, the 1928 plane swing, before you leave.

adventure.title: Montserrat and the Sant Joan Funicular
adventure.description: Take the rack railway up a mountain of stone fingers, then ride the funicular higher still to a hermitage trail with nothing above you but sky.
adventure.bonus: Walk to Sant Jeroni, the true summit, instead of stopping at the monastery.

adventure.title: Kayak and Snorkel the Costa Brava Coves
adventure.description: Paddle into limestone calas an hour north of the city where the water goes glass-clear and the crowds simply do not reach.
adventure.bonus: Swim into at least one sea cave.

adventure.title: Swim at Sant Sebastià and Walk the Breakwater
adventure.description: Start with a cold morning swim at the quietest end of Barceloneta, then walk the concrete arm out to where the city looks like a postcard someone dropped in the sea.
adventure.bonus: Get in before 9am, when the water is still yours.

adventure.title: Escape to Sitges on the Rodalies Train
adventure.description: Forty minutes down the coast and you are in a whitewashed town with seventeen beaches, a hilltop church and a completely different pace.
adventure.bonus: Walk past the church to the quieter beaches on the far side.

adventure.title: Dawn Walk on the Carretera de les Aigües
adventure.description: Follow a flat dirt balcony cut into the Collserola hillside while the city wakes up 300 metres below you.
adventure.bonus: Get there before the first jogger passes you.

adventure.title: Sunset Sail Out of Port Vell
adventure.description: Slip out past the breakwater on a catamaran as the light goes orange on the Barceloneta towers behind you.
adventure.bonus: Take the helm when they offer it.

adventure.title: Helicopter Flight Over the Barcelona Coastline
adventure.description: Lift off from the port and see Gaudí's spires, the grid of the Eixample and the whole curve of the coast in one sweep.
adventure.bonus: Ask for the seat next to the pilot.

adventure.title: Sunrise Run Up Montjuïc
adventure.description: Run the winding paths up Montjuïc hill before the city wakes, finishing at a viewpoint over the harbor.
adventure.bonus: Race the sunrise to the top

adventure.title: Surf Lesson at Barceloneta Beach
adventure.description: Catch your first waves with a local instructor right off the city's main beach.
adventure.bonus: Stand up on the first try or the fifth, doesn't matter

adventure.title: Cable Car to Montjuïc Castle
adventure.description: Glide over the harbor by cable car to a 17th-century hilltop fortress with sweeping views of the port.
adventure.bonus: Ride standing at the front window

adventure.title: Cycle the Beachfront to Poblenou
adventure.description: Rent a bike and ride the flat coastal path from Barceloneta past four beaches to Poblenou.
adventure.bonus: Stop for a swim halfway through

adventure.title: Sagrada Família Guided Tour
adventure.description: Walk beneath Gaudí's still-unfinished masterpiece with a guide who explains what the guidebooks skip.
adventure.bonus: Find the shell staircase and don't rush it

adventure.title: Stand-Up Paddleboard the Old Port
adventure.description: Rent a paddleboard and glide across the calm water of Port Vell with the city skyline behind you.
adventure.bonus: Try to stay dry for the whole hour

culture.title: MACBA and the Skaters Outside It
culture.description: See the contemporary collection inside, then sit on the white plaza where Barcelona's skate scene has been grinding the ledges since the nineties.
culture.bonus: Stay outside long enough to see someone land something.

culture.title: A Night at the Liceu
culture.description: Take a seat in the gilded opera house on La Rambla that has burned down twice and been rebuilt exactly as it was, both times.
culture.bonus: Book a box, however cheap, over a stall seat.

culture.title: The Hospital That Looks Like a Palace
culture.description: Walk the pavilions and tiled tunnels of Sant Pau, a working hospital until 2009 and the largest art nouveau site in the world.
culture.bonus: Go down into the underground tunnels between pavilions.

culture.title: Watch the Castellers Build a Human Tower
culture.description: Find a colla's open rehearsal and watch a hundred people build a nine-storey tower out of each other, with a child climbing to the top.
culture.bonus: Stay for the moment the tower comes down.

culture.title: La Pedrera After Dark
culture.description: Walk Gaudí's chimney-forest rooftop at night, with the warrior chimneys lit and the city humming below.
culture.bonus: Stay on the roof until they ask you to leave.

culture.title: Casa Batlló, Top to Roof
culture.description: Walk through Gaudí's bone-and-scale house on Passeig de Gràcia and come out on a roof terrace shaped like a dragon's back.
culture.bonus: Find the room with no straight line in it.

culture.title: The Stained Glass of Palau de la Música
culture.description: Take the tour of a modernista concert hall built almost entirely of coloured glass, where the ceiling is an inverted sun.
culture.bonus: Stand directly under the skylight and look straight up.

culture.title: Miró on the Hill
culture.description: Spend an afternoon with primary colours and hanging mobiles at the foundation Joan Miró designed for his own work, halfway up Montjuïc.
culture.bonus: Go out to the roof terrace most people miss.

foodie.title: Cava Cellars in the Penedès
foodie.description: Take the train into the vineyards to drink the sparkling wine Catalonia makes better than anyone, in the cellars where it ages underground.
foodie.bonus: Learn what gran reserva actually requires before you taste.

foodie.title: The Tasting Menu at Disfrutar
foodie.description: Give up an entire evening to thirty courses of edible sleight-of-hand from a team that trained at elBulli.
foodie.bonus: Book the kitchen table if it is free.

foodie.title: Vermouth and Tinned Fish at Bodega 1900
foodie.description: Sit at a small bar in Sant Antoni and eat conservas and pickles the way a Catalan grandfather would, with house vermouth over ice.
foodie.bonus: Let the bartender choose your tin.

foodie.title: Seafood at Els Pescadors in Poblenou
foodie.description: Eat rice and whole fish on a quiet square shaded by ombú trees, in the neighbourhood restaurant locals kept to themselves for decades.
foodie.bonus: Order the fish of the day without asking the price.

foodie.title: Breakfast Under the Wave at Santa Caterina
foodie.description: Eat at a market counter beneath a rippling technicolour roof, two minutes and a world away from the Boqueria crush.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever the person next to you is having.

foodie.title: Patatas Bravas at Bar Tomás
foodie.description: Ride the metro up to Sarrià for the plate of fried potatoes that locals will argue is the only one in the city that counts.
foodie.bonus: Get them amb toc, with the extra kick.

foodie.title: Thick Chocolate at Granja Viader
foodie.description: Duck into an 1870s dairy off La Rambla for a cup of chocolate so thick the spoon stands up in it.
foodie.bonus: Order the suís, with the cream on top.

foodie.title: The Bomba at La Cova Fumada
foodie.description: Order the potato-and-meat grenade that was invented in this unmarked Barceloneta doorway, standing at a marble counter under fluorescent light.

foodie.title: Tapas Hopping at Quimet & Quimet
foodie.description: Squeeze into this legendary standing-room bodega for montaditos piled with the best tinned seafood in the city.
foodie.bonus: Stay standing the whole time, like a local

foodie.title: Paella on the Beach at Barceloneta
foodie.description: Dig into a pan of proper Valencian-style paella at a beachfront chiringuito with sand between your toes.
foodie.bonus: Order it for two and share the socarrat

foodie.title: Breakfast Crawl at La Boqueria
foodie.description: Weave through Barcelona's most famous market for fresh juice, jamón, and a stool at the counter bars.

foodie.title: Vermouth Hour in El Born
foodie.description: Join the Sunday-afternoon ritual of a chilled glass of vermouth and a plate of olives at a corner bar.
foodie.bonus: Order the vermut de grifo, on tap

social.title: Absinthe at Bar Marsella
social.description: Drink in a peeling 1820s room with dusty bottles nobody has moved in a century, where the house pour still arrives with sugar and a slotted spoon.

social.title: Sunday Vermut on Plaça del Sol
social.description: Join the Gràcia ritual: a bitter vermouth with an olive and an orange slice, on a square full of people doing exactly the same thing.
social.bonus: Stay for a second round and talk to the next table.

social.title: Cocktails at Paradiso, Behind the Pastrami Fridge
social.description: Walk through a sandwich shop's refrigerator door into a barrel-vaulted room that has been called the best bar in the world.
social.bonus: Order the drink that arrives with smoke, no questions asked.

social.title: Matchday at Camp Nou
social.description: Ninety minutes inside the largest stadium in Europe, with the anthem going up from every side before kickoff.
social.bonus: Learn the words to Cant del Barça before you go.

social.title: Late Jazz at Jamboree
social.description: Go down into a stone cellar on Plaça Reial for the late set, where the ceiling is low and the band is close enough to touch.
social.bonus: Take the second set, not the first.

social.title: Nasty Mondays at Sala Apolo
social.description: Start the week wrong in a red-velvet 1940s dance hall where the indie-rock night has been running since before most of the room was born.
social.bonus: Stay until the encore track everyone knows.

social.title: Pintxo Crawl Down Carrer Blai
social.description: Work down a pedestrian street in Poble-sec where every bar charges about two euros a skewer and keeps score with your toothpicks.
social.bonus: Four bars minimum, one pintxo each, no repeats.

social.title: Salsa Night at Antilla BCN
social.description: Take the free early lesson, then stay while the floor fills with people who have been dancing here for twenty years.

social.title: Pub Crawl Through El Born
social.description: Hit a rotating lineup of tucked-away bars in El Born's narrow streets with a group that keeps growing.
social.bonus: Buy the next stranger at the bar a drink

social.title: Flamenco Show at Palau Dalmases
social.description: Catch an intimate flamenco performance in a 17th-century palace lit almost entirely by candlelight.
social.bonus: Sit at the front row, close enough to feel it

social.title: Night Out at Razzmatazz
social.description: Dance across five different rooms and music styles under one roof at Barcelona's most iconic club.
social.bonus: Try all five rooms before midnight

social.title: Rooftop Drinks with a Sagrada Família View
social.description: Order a cocktail on a rooftop terrace with Gaudí's spires lit up just blocks away.
social.bonus: Toast to the skyline with someone you just met

chill.title: First Light at Bogatell Beach
chill.description: Walk down before the beach bars open and have a kilometre of sand and a flat sea more or less to yourself.
chill.bonus: Stay off your phone the whole time.

chill.title: Row the Lake at Parc de la Ciutadella
chill.description: Take a rowboat out under the ridiculous baroque waterfall Gaudí helped build as a student, then lie on the grass until the light goes.
chill.bonus: Row a full lap without hitting anyone.

chill.title: Sunset at the Mirador del Migdia
chill.description: Climb the back of Montjuïc to a scrappy pine-shaded terrace bar where the sun goes down over the sea and nobody is in a hurry.
chill.bonus: Bring something to share and stay until the lights come on.

chill.title: Get Lost in the Laberint d'Horta
chill.description: Wander an 18th-century cypress maze in the city's oldest garden, where almost no tourist ever bothers to go.
chill.bonus: Reach the centre without backtracking once.

chill.title: Candlelit Baths at Aire Ancient Baths
chill.description: Move between hot, cold and salt pools in a converted Born warehouse lit almost entirely by candles, with your phone locked away.
chill.bonus: Do the full circuit in order, cold plunge included.

chill.title: Coffee and Croissant at Hofmann Pastisseria
chill.description: Sit with the mascarpone croissant that pastry students queue for, in a tiny Born shop that takes laminated dough extremely seriously.
chill.bonus: Eat it standing at the counter, still warm.

chill.title: Wander Park Güell at Opening Hour
chill.description: Get inside Gaudí's fairy-tale park before the tour buses arrive and have the tiled terraces nearly to yourself.
chill.bonus: Find the mosaic lizard before the crowds do

chill.title: Afternoon at Museu Picasso
chill.description: Trace Picasso's early years through room after room of his formative work in a quiet Gothic mansion.
chill.bonus: Pick one painting and just sit with it for five minutes

chill.title: Slow Stroll Through the Gothic Quarter
chill.description: Get pleasantly lost in the medieval maze of Barri Gòtic, from Plaça Reial to the cathedral cloister.
chill.bonus: Take the alley you'd normally skip

8ball.title: Get Off at a Metro Stop You've Never Heard Of
8ball.description: Ride the green line, pick a station name you cannot pronounce, get out and spend two hours wherever you land.
8ball.bonus: Eat wherever the queue is longest.

8ball.title: Let the Bartender Decide
8ball.description: Walk into a bar you have never been to, tell them you will drink whatever they think you should, and do it.
8ball.bonus: Do it twice, at two different bars.
